            What to do here Focus on who was involved, what happened, when it happened, and how it affected the complainant. If the exact date or wording is uncertain, save the best current version and improve it later.

            Start with the story the complainant can tell clearly today

            Use plain language. Best estimate is okay. If dates or exact wording are uncertain, capture the best current version now and come back with corroboration in the Evidence stage.

            Ask for sequence What happened first, what happened next, and how soon after the report or complaint did the harm occur?
            Name the actors Capture who made the decision, who knew about the report or complaint, and who communicated what happened next.
            Leave room for uncertainty Approximate dates and incomplete recall are acceptable at intake if they are marked for later corroboration. You can skip and return.

            What to do here Add the records or witness details most likely to strengthen the missing parts of the complaint. Every saved item should answer the question: what does this help prove?

            What counts as helpful support

            Prefer concrete sources: emails, messages, witness accounts, meeting notes, timeline records, HR filings, performance reviews, and anything that helps anchor protected activity, employer knowledge, causation, or damages.

            The next proof move will appear here once review data loads. The workspace will point to the weakest supported element so the next testimony or document directly strengthens the complaint record.

                      Package

                      Python package imports

                      from complaint_generator import ComplaintWorkspaceService, create_review_surface_app, export_complaint_docx
from complaint_generator.mcp import handle_jsonrpc_message

service = ComplaintWorkspaceService()
session = service.get_session("did:key:example")
docx_artifact = export_complaint_docx("did:key:example", service=service)
                      CLI

                      Python CLI

                      complaint-workspace session --user-id did:key:example
complaint-generator-workspace session --user-id did:key:example
complaint-workspace answer --user-id did:key:example --question-id protected_activity --answer-text "Reported discrimination to HR"
complaint-generator-workspace generate --user-id did:key:example --requested-relief "Back pay|Injunctive relief"
complaint-workspace run-gmail-duckdb-pipeline --user-id did:key:example --address hr@example.com --complaint-keyword retaliation
complaint-workspace search-email-duckdb --index-path artifacts/email_corpus.duckdb --query "termination retaliation"
complaint-workspace workspace-data-schema --user-id did:key:example
complaint-workspace migrate-legacy-workspace-data --user-id did:key:example --output-dir artifacts/workspace-dataset
complaint-workspace export-markdown --user-id did:key:example
complaint-workspace export-docx --user-id did:key:example
complaint-workspace export-pdf --user-id did:key:example
complaint-workspace browser-audit artifacts/ui-audit/browser-audit
                      MCP

                      MCP stdio server

                      complaint-generator-mcp
complaint-mcp-server
tool: complaint.get_workspace_data_schema
tool: complaint.migrate_legacy_workspace_data
tool: complaint.export_complaint_docx
tool: complaint.run_browser_audit
                      Browser SDK

                      JavaScript MCP SDK

                      const client = new window.ComplaintMcpSdk.ComplaintMcpClient();
const bootstrap = await client.bootstrapWorkspace();
await client.callTool('complaint.review_case', { user_id: bootstrap.did });
await client.runGmailDuckdbPipeline({ user_id: bootstrap.did, addresses: ['hr@example.com'] });
await client.searchEmailDuckdb({ index_path: 'artifacts/email_corpus.duckdb', query: 'termination retaliation' });
await client.getWorkspaceDataSchema(bootstrap.did);
await client.migrateLegacyWorkspaceData(bootstrap.did, 'artifacts/workspace-dataset');
await client.exportComplaintMarkdown(bootstrap.did);
await client.exportComplaintDocx(bootstrap.did);
await client.exportComplaintPdf(bootstrap.did);
await client.runBrowserAudit({ screenshot_dir: 'artifacts/ui-audit/browser-audit' });

                      Agentic UX Review

                      Use the MCP JavaScript SDK to call the complaint.review_ui tool, run the screenshot audit flow, and review the current workspace with an actor/critic lens that checks trauma-informed language, clearer next steps, stronger complaint-handling guidance, and whether the full complaint-generator feature set is actually discoverable and usable.

                      What to do here Use this stage when you want the system to critique the interface itself. It captures screenshots, reviews the UI, and can run a closed-loop optimization cycle without leaving the shared dashboard.

                      How this loop works

                      The workflow captures Playwright screenshots, sends them through the multimodal router when available, and returns recommendations that keep intake, evidence, review, mediator coaching, draft, package exports, CLI tools, MCP tools, browser SDK paths, and the actor/critic optimizer itself aligned while the UI evolves.

                      The default audit walks the landing, chat, profile, workspace intake, evidence, review, mediator handoff, draft, CLI + MCP, and builder surfaces before the actor/critic optimizer proposes a patch.
